programs.name: Disabled Veteran Exemption

ptRequired.quote: permanently and totally disabled as a result of military service and entitled to veterans' benefits at the 100% rate

summary.current: Full exemption (MCL 211.7b) at 100% rating, VA Individual Unemployability, OR receipt of VA Specially Adapted Housing assistance
summary.correct: Full exemption (MCL 211.7b) for a Michigan-resident veteran who is (i) permanently and totally disabled and paid at the 100% rate, OR (ii) rated individually unemployable, OR (iii) receiving/received SAH or SHA assistance. A 100% schedular rating that is not P&T is not one of the three routes.
summary.quote: (i) ... entitled to veterans' benefits at the 100% rate. (ii) ... pecuniary assistance due to disability for specially adapted housing. (iii) ... rated by the United States Department of Veterans Affairs as individually unemployable.

survivingSpouse.quote: A surviving spouse of a disabled veteran who, immediately before death, was eligible ... continues as long as the surviving spouse does not remarry

type.quote: Real property used and owned as a homestead by a disabled veteran ... is exempt from the collection of taxes under this act

programs.effectiveChanges: No 2024, 2025 or 2026 Public Act amends MCL 211.7b or 211.7c (history lines end at 2023 PA 150 and 2023 PA 151; the MCL site is current through PA 114 of 2026). The 'January 1, 2025' date in the statute is the start of one-time filing under 211.7c, not a 2025 amendment. Form 5107 was re-issued Rev. 03-26 (approved April 7, 2026) with the same three eligibility routes.
programs.note: The lead about '2025 changes to MCL 211.7b/7c' resolves to: no statutory change; the only 2025-26 activity is the operational switch to no-reapplication filing and the April 2026 form revision. The IU route is the TDIU hook (a TDIU veteran with a sub-100% combined rating qualifies).

programs.name: Homestead Property Tax Credit

exemptionValue.quote: Homestead Property Tax Credit ... $165,400 ... $71,500 ... $1,900 ... $70,501 - $71,500 (Tax Year 2025 Information page)

incomeLimit.quote: Tax Year 2025: total household resources limit $71,500; taxable value limit $165,400; maximum credit $1,900

details.current: Property tax credit up to $1,800 on Michigan primary residence ... Renters may also qualify for credit up to $1,800.
details.correct: Refundable credit up to $1,900 (TY2025; indexed annually) for homeowners and renters; total household resources must be at or under $71,500 and homestead taxable value at or under $165,400. Veterans with a service-connected disability and surviving spouses file MI-1040CR-2 if it yields more.
details.quote: MI-1040CR-2 (Homestead Property Tax Credit Claim for Veterans and Blind People)

nonVeteran.quote: You have Total Household Resources (THR) under a specified amount adjusted annually.

programs.effectiveChanges: TY2026 figures (max credit, THR and taxable-value caps) are indexed and will post with the 2026 MI-1040CR in January 2027; TY2025 values are the latest published.
programs.note: This is a general, income-tested income-tax credit, not a veteran exemption; it should carry nonVeteran:true (or be excluded from veteran savings) the way MN's general exclusion is. The stale '$1,800' in `details` should become $1,900.

summary: MCL 211.7b/7c have not been amended since 2023; the exemption remains full, with P&T-at-100%, IU, or SAH/SHA as the three routes, so the row should set ptRequired:true with IU/SAH alternates rather than imply any 100% rating qualifies. The homestead credit figures ($1,900 / $71,500 / $165,400 for TY2025) are confirmed on michigan.gov but the row's `details` still says $1,800 and the credit should be flagged nonVeteran; the file's 1.54% tax rate is 0.35 pp above the Tax Foundation 2024 figure.
